Course Policies

Attendance and Participation
[State your attendance expectations. If participation is graded, explain how it is evaluated.]


Late Work
[State your late work policy clearly — for example: “Assignments submitted late will lose 10% per day. Extensions are granted upon request before the deadline.” Be explicit about how to request an extension.]


Use of AI Tools
[State your policy on the use of large language models and generative AI tools for coursework. Be specific about which tasks permit or prohibit AI assistance, and what constitutes academic dishonesty in this context.]


Academic Integrity
All work submitted in this course must be your own. Collaboration is [encouraged / not permitted] on [specific assignments]. Violations of academic integrity will be handled in accordance with [Institution]’s Academic Integrity Policy.


Accessibility and Accommodations
[Institution] is committed to providing an accessible learning environment for all students. Students who require accommodations should contact the Disability Services Office and provide documentation. Please share your accommodation letter with me as early in the semester as possible so we can arrange support promptly.
If you encounter accessibility barriers in any course materials — including this website — please contact me directly at email@institution.edu so I can provide an accessible alternative.
This course website is built to meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA. If you find a barrier that prevents you from accessing content, please let me know.


Student Wellbeing
Graduate and undergraduate students alike can experience significant stress and mental health challenges. [Institution] offers Counseling and Psychological Services. You are always welcome to speak with me if you are struggling.


Communication
The best way to reach me is by email at email@institution.edu. I aim to respond within [24/48] hours on business days. For questions that others may share, please consider posting to [the course discussion forum / Discord / Piazza] so classmates can benefit from the answer.

title: Welcome to the Course!
text:
Skip to main content




Welcome to PUBA 720! Here is what to do before we meet for the first time:

Read the syllabus — Review the Syllabus carefully, especially the policies section.
Check the schedule — Look over the Schedule to plan your semester.
Install software — Follow the setup instructions on the Resources page.
Complete Exercise 1 — The first exercise is due [date]. See Assignments for details.

If you have any questions before the semester begins, feel free to email me at email@institution.edu.
Looking forward to working with you this semester!
